One ordinary day at a community center, a situation involving a family responsibility begins to change the plans for the afternoon. sentences.html: Mateo is 15–16 years old and studies in Medellín. One ordinary day at a community center, a situation involving a family responsibility begins to change the plans for the afternoon.
Isabella is nearby and notices that Mateo is paying close attention to what is happening.
The first reaction seems simple, but the details matter because the problem is really about cooperation and priorities.
This week, Mateo becomes a part-time caregiver for a grandparent.
The moment feels personal, but it also connects with school life, family expectations, and the way young people communicate today.
A compromise lets Mateo help at home and see friends later.

sentences.html: The situation becomes harder when family responsibilities interrupt a personal plan. Mateo feels pressure to react quickly.
Instead of having all the facts, the students hear different versions of what happened.
Isabella suggests checking the information before blaming anyone or making a promise that cannot be kept.
The group is meeting after class, and they are going to compare several options.
Isabella reminds Mateo that asking for help can be a responsible decision when the situation is unclear.
Mateo listens carefully before answering, because one missing detail can change the meaning of the whole situation.
It is hard to juggle school, home and friends.
Good friends are flexible when a family need appears.

quiz.question: Who notices that Mateo is paying close attention to what is happening?
options: Diego
Tomás
Isabella
Sara
quiz.answer: Isabella

quiz.question: Why does Mateo listen carefully before answering?
options: Because one missing detail can change the meaning of the situation.
Because nobody else is paying attention.
Because he does not understand Spanish.
Because the teacher prohibits talking.
quiz.answer: Because one missing detail can change the meaning of the situation.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the question “What do you know for sure, and what are you only assuming?”
options: To give the students a grammar exercise.
To end the conversation quickly.
To blame one student for the problem.
To help the students separate evidence from emotion.
quiz.answer: To help the students separate evidence from emotion.

quiz.question: In “Instead of having all the facts, the students hear different versions of what happened,” the expression “instead of” shows that…
options: the students have all the information they need
the students get rumors in place of complete information
the versions are all exactly the same
the facts arrive after a long time
quiz.answer: the students get rumors in place of complete information

quiz.question: Which sentence best expresses the main lesson of the text?
options: The fastest reaction is always the best one.
Good decisions come from evidence, not from pressure.
Popular opinions are usually correct.
It is better to stay silent when there is a problem.
quiz.answer: Good decisions come from evidence, not from pressure.
